title: Experiences in women with gynecological sarcoma: A qualitative interview study with mixed-methods analysis of REGSA data
summary: Gynaecological sarcomas often take a long time to diagnose. The aim of this study is to gain a better understanding of the symptoms experienced by patients at the onset of the disease, how they experience the path to diagnosis, and the stresses they face during this time. Interviews are conducted with patients in which they describe their experiences. In addition, depending on the interview results, existing registry data will be evaluated in order to systematically examine typical symptoms and processes leading up to diagnosis. The results should contribute to improving diagnosis and providing more targeted support to those affected during this phase.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of uterus, part unspecified

interventions.name:
Non-interventional mixed-methods study with qualitative, semi-structured, individual interviews to record the subjective stress experiences during the diagnostic phase of patients with gynaecological sarcomas. 

This is supplemented by quantitative data analysis based on the data recorded in the R

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients diagnosed with gynaecological sarcomas
- Patients participating in REGSA
- Written consent available and capable of giving consent
- Language: sufficient knowledge of German or English
- Willingness to participate in a 30-60 minute interview
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of capacity to give consent
- Medical reasons why participation would not be justifiable (e.g. advanced stage of disease with severe symptoms)
- Withdrawal of consent
- Excessive psychological stress
- Lack of language skills, making participation in the study and understanding of information/interview questions impossible
